loadout.attribute: Full STR or Full Armor/HP (Amya OP). General Hero Guide's heavy table confirms: "Maul: Full HP/Armor or Full STR". Official 2021 guide: most Maulers invest the bulk of their Attribute points into Armour and Toughness, simply to maximise hit points and be able to soak up all that incoming damage - it's unnecessary to invest fully in increased Strength, but those that do might find the investment really pays off. - Amya

Mighty Mjölnir is the likely fourth slot - JUBAI frames it as the learner-recommended mobility/engage tool - but this is an inference from the source text, not a verbatim "core loadout" line. - Amya / JUBAI (inferred)

builds.name: Flameshackle
builds.summary: Amya OP's only named "Best Armour" for Maul (no Stoneguard alternative offered in this source, unlike Shortsword's dual framing). Read as the dps/farm pick given Flameshackle's unit-damage-oriented 3pc/5pc text and the house block-break interaction.

builds.name: Hammer of the Gods
builds.summary: "Not required... but good to have it in certain meta" (Amya OP). Benefits Mighty Mjölnir's cooldown (2pc) and charging-skill stamina cost (4pc) per the dated 2021 guide text.

builds.name: Mobility-lean
builds.summary: JUBAI's framing: prioritize Mighty Mjölnir, recommended especially for players learning the class; escape-capable via the charge.
builds.forWhom: Recommended for players learning the class.

builds.name: Full Strength
builds.summary: Official 2021 guide: unnecessary given Blunt damage's general effectiveness, but "really pays off" for players who invest anyway. Amya OP lists it as a co-equal option with Full Armor/HP rather than a beginner-discouraged pick (contrast with the Shortsword file's "Not for beginners" framing of its own Full Strength variant - Maul's OP doesn't carry that same caution).

matchups.why: Paladins get "crunched" by maul-type weapons; a dismount-stun chain can lock down the whole unit, especially in the tight block/shield formation rather than spread. Ranked as one of the unit's two biggest practical threats (alongside cavalry). [external video, HandBananaPvP]
"the easiest way to deal with a Berserker player is to kill the controller directly" - the creator specifically calls out Maul players doing this. [external video, crazymetalord]

Amya's Longbow guide coaches using Light-footed's brief invincibility specifically to dodge "deadly ultimates like Dual Blades or Maul's heavy strikes" - one of only two hero threats a Longbow player is taught to evade this way. Source doesn't say which Maul ultimate.

"heavy armoured heroes with low-mobility weapon classes such as the maul and the poleaxe (without Rough Justice) are at a disadvantage when dueling with musket users." [wiki, Musket "Playing Against Musket"]
No explicit Amya/JUBAI list of which units a Maul player should bring in their own warband. [GAP: vets/house question, same honest-gap pattern as the shortsword file's equivalent section]

techniques.name: Animation canceling
steps: Training room: try roll-canceling, dismount-canceling and blocking on every skill to learn which are cancelable.
techniques.rhythm: Amya: EVERY CLASS CAN DO IT! - Blocking is the primary cancel; roll canceling interrupts full spells, dismounts, and creates movement otherwise impossible. Costs extra stamina.

techniques.name: Active blocking
steps: it can be BROKEN and stagger you
techniques.rhythm: Don't get "Block checked" - Being an active blocker prevents undesired skills landing on you.

techniques.name: Horse-whistle CC immunity
steps: Time the whistle on the enemy CC
you take damage but no CC
techniques.rhythm: bugs out with PIN/LOCK skills, so care

techniques.name: Walk into braced units
steps: Walk (don't sprint) into their minimal range
techniques.rhythm: brace damage scales with your speed towards them - For braced units like Forte, Halberds, Phalanx - niche: enemy hero outnumbered, unaware or afk.

techniques.name: Dash-auto-attack-animation-cancel
steps: side-roll the instant the damage pop-up appears
techniques.rhythm: OP: the class's core skill expression; rest of the kit "does not require a lot of skill" by comparison - OP: learn to dash-auto-attack-animation-cancel and perfect it.

gameplay.text: Spells are either "charged" or combo'd off one of the two combo-starters (Mighty Mjolnir / Mountain Breaker). Both ultimates are viable (can also be played with no ult), though JUBAI personally prefers Forge of War for its high-range heavy CC and CC-recovery (no-mobility builds are also playable).

roleLabel: Maul is a bruiser class offering mobility and constant DPS/high burst depending on build.

positioning.intro: Where to be during a fight:

bullets.text: Maelstrom and the dive combo point at flanking/backline dives (arty, exotics, isolated pike), not static frontline holding.
Forge of War is explicitly good "in frontline-to-frontline, flanking, and 1v1s".
Bonebreaker ("farm frontlines") is called out-of-meta specifically because standing in the frontline to use it leaves the player exposed.
Overall the class reads as a mobile bruiser/hero-hunter via the dash-auto-attack-cancel loop, not a static tank.
Core skill expression is the dash-auto-attack-animation-cancel loop (auto-attack, side-roll the instant the damage number pops, repeat) - the class's primary skill ceiling per the OP.
Mountain Breaker and Mighty Mjölnir both grant a 26% buff to whatever's combo'd after them - plan the rotation around this.
Titanic Shockwave upgrades Earthsplitter from "decent" to "truly meta," turning its knockback into a big-area CC tool.
Forge of War's Concussed phase can stop a mounted target, but they can cancel it by self-dismounting - don't assume the CC is guaranteed to land through a horse escape.
Maelstrom's on-cast CC immunity plus its stamina-scalable damage make it the class's premier dive tool against squishy backline targets (arty/exotics/pike) rather than a frontline trading tool.
Grab/Strike and Grapple's real value in the current (out-of-meta-as-a-main-pick) state is situational: trap-and-drop wall climbers on offense, or CC-then-grab them on defense.

bullets.lead: Enemy-side counter-play read (external matchup evidence, not Amya/JUBAI):
bullets.text: Maul is specifically feared for dismount-stun lockdown on clustered/braced melee units and for hunting down exposed unit controllers - the class's own playstyle advice is implicitly "look for exactly those openings" rather than trading in the open frontline.

statSpreads.note: Official 2021 guide: unnecessary given Blunt damage's general effectiveness, but "really pays off" for players who invest anyway - not a beginner-discouraged pick per Amya (unlike Shortsword's own Full Strength variant).

combos.name: Combo starter chain
combos.note: Combo-starters each grant a 26% buff to the next skill used. Bonebreaker is the only skill playable stand-alone/charged, since it skips the 26% debuff and uses under 50% stamina.

combos.name: Dive
combos.note: Maelstrom grants CC immunity on cast; target artillery, exotics, or isolated pike units - not built for frontline-to-frontline trading, more of a flanking tool.

combos.name: Forge of War two-phase CC
combos.note: Can stop a mounted enemy (though they can escape by self-dismounting before it lands). Good in frontline-to-frontline, flanking, and 1v1s.

combos.name: Titanic Shockwave upgrade
combos.note: Turns Earthsplitter's knockback hit into "a big-area CC" per JUBAI - meta-defining for the skill.

combos.name: Grab utility play
steps: trap-and-drop wall climbers (offense) or CC-then-grab climbers (defense)
combos.note: "A bit coinflip since teamplay will disrupt it but not always the case."

combos.name: Flameshackle block-break
combos.note: House [jc008titanSQ]: "Flameshackle armor set bonus works on maul earthsplitter 1 and dismount" (does not work on earthsplitter 3rd stage or ult) - "so basically you can block break everything with the malestorm hit... works better than on bastard sword."
